The worshipper laid his hand on the animal's head, and it was accepted for him. How does this point to Jesus taking our place?
The burnt offering was "a pleasing aroma to the Lord." What does it mean to offer your whole self to God?
Offerings could be from the herd, the flock or birds. What does this show about God making a way for everyone?
The grain offering came from everyday food. How can you offer your everyday life to God?
Salt was added to every offering, "the salt of the covenant." What does this teach about God's lasting faithfulness?
Firstfruits were brought to God. How can you give God the first and best?
The peace offering was shared, a sign of fellowship with God. What does peace with God mean to you?
Every detail was given by God. Why does God tell us how to approach him rather than leaving it to us?
Even unintentional sins needed atonement. What does this show about the seriousness of sin?
When the whole community sinned, they brought an offering together. How can a church seek forgiveness together?
"He shall be forgiven." What does it mean to you that forgiveness is possible?
People were to confess the sin they had committed. Why does confession matter?
Those who could not afford a lamb could bring birds or flour. What does this show about God's grace to the poor?
Guilt offerings included restitution. Is there anything you need to make right with someone?
Wronging a neighbour was also a sin against the Lord. How does this change how you see wrongs against others?
The fire on the altar was never to go out. What keeps your devotion to God burning?
The sin offering was "most holy." What does this show about the holiness of atonement?
Peace offerings could be given in thanksgiving. What are you thankful to God for today?
Some offerings were freewill offerings. What would you freely offer God?
These were the laws for drawing near to God. How do we draw near to God now through Jesus?
Aaron and his sons were washed and clothed for service. How does God prepare us to serve him?
The anointing oil set the tabernacle and priests apart. What does it mean to be set apart for God?
The priests did all that the Lord commanded. Why is obedience part of worship?
Moses said, "Today the Lord will appear to you." How do you expect God to meet you?
Fire came from the Lord and the people shouted and fell on their faces. How do you respond to God's glory?
Nadab and Abihu offered unauthorised fire and died. What does this teach about approaching God on his terms?
God says, "Among those who are near me I will be sanctified." What does honouring God as holy look like?
The priests were to distinguish between holy and common. How can you tell what honours God?
Moses accepted Aaron's honest explanation. What does this show about grace in hard moments?
God set apart some foods as clean and unclean. Why do you think God taught Israel to make distinctions in daily life?
"Be holy, for I am holy." What does holiness look like in your daily life?
God wanted his people to distinguish between clean and unclean. How does Jesus make us clean?
Even birth required purification. What does this show about the need for cleansing in all of life?
A poor mother could offer two birds, as Mary did after Jesus' birth. What does this show about Jesus' humble beginnings?
The priest carefully examined skin diseases. What does this show about care for the sick?
The person with leprosy had to live alone and cry "Unclean!" How does Jesus' touch of lepers change this picture?
There was a ceremony for one who was cleansed. How does it feel to be restored after being an outsider?
The healed person was brought back into the community. Who needs to be welcomed back in your community?
Even houses could be cleansed. What in your home or life might need God's cleansing?
God gave careful instructions for everyday cleanness. What does this show about God's concern for all of life?
God wanted to keep them from defiling his dwelling place. What does God's presence among his people require?
Aaron could only enter the Most Holy Place once a year. How does Jesus give us access to God?
The high priest made atonement for himself and the people. What does atonement mean?
The scapegoat carried their sins away into the wilderness. How does this picture what Christ did for you?
The people rested and humbled themselves on the Day of Atonement. How can you respond to God's forgiveness?
"The life of the flesh is in the blood... it is the blood that makes atonement." How does this point to the cross?
God's people were to treat life with reverence. What does this teach about valuing life?
God says, "You shall not do as they do in Egypt or Canaan." What cultural pressures do you face?
"You shall keep my statutes... if a person does them, he shall live by them." What does God's law show about life?
God called Israel to be different from the nations around them. How can you be distinct without being proud?
"You shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy." What would holiness look like in your relationships?
God told them to leave the edges of the field for the poor. How can you leave room for others in need?
"You shall love your neighbour as yourself." Who is your neighbour this week?
Treat the foreigner as a native and love him as yourself. How can you welcome those from other places?
"I am the Lord who sanctifies you." What does it mean that God makes you holy?
God says, "I have separated you from the peoples, that you should be mine." What does it mean to belong to God?
The priests were to be holy because they offered the bread of their God. How does serving God call for holiness?
The priests' physical wholeness pointed to God's perfection. How does Jesus, our perfect high priest, fulfil this?
Offerings were to be without blemish. What does it mean to give God your best?
"I am the Lord who sanctifies you, who brought you out of Egypt." How does remembering God's rescue lead to obedience?
The weekly Sabbath was a holy gathering. How do you keep a rhythm of rest and worship?
Passover and firstfruits remembered God's rescue and provision. How do you celebrate God's goodness?
At harvest they were to leave gleanings for the poor. How can your blessings bless others?
At the Feast of Booths they lived in shelters to remember the wilderness. What helps you remember God's past care?
The lamp was to burn regularly before the Lord. What keeps your devotion steady?
Bread was set before the Lord every Sabbath. What does this teach about ongoing fellowship with God?
"You shall have the same rule for the sojourner and for the native." What does this show about justice?
Even the land was to have a Sabbath rest. What does this teach about trusting God's provision?
In the year of Jubilee everyone returned to their property. What does this show about God's heart for restoration?
God says, "The land is mine. For you are strangers and sojourners with me." How should this shape how you hold possessions?
God says to help a poor brother and not to rule over him harshly. How can you help someone in need?
God promised to walk among them and be their God. What does it mean that God walks with you?
God says, "I have broken the bars of your yoke and made you walk erect." What has God freed you from?
Even after judgement, God would remember his covenant. What does this show about God's faithfulness?
Vows were taken seriously before God. How seriously do you take your promises?
"Every tithe... is holy to the Lord." What does it mean to give to God first?
